answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring every identity to lock a unique physical sample of cedar wood carrying a distinct walnut inlay and a measured saffron pigment patch. Peers verify it with multi-view hashes and spectral scans that bind the sample to one address only. A farmer cannot reuse one plank for many clones; each fake needs its own real object, shipping, and non-refundable verification stake that is slashed on reuse or mismatch, so the cost of the nth identity grows with scarce materials and logistics rather than free software copies.
